title: Diwali: The Festival of Lights Celebrated Across Cultures
excerpt: A celebration of light, joy, and togetherness for millions worldwide.
body:
Diwali, also known as the Festival of Lights, is one of the most significant festivals in Hindu culture, symbolizing the victory of light over darkness and good over evil. It is celebrated by millions around the world, marking the return of Lord Rama to Ayodhya after defeating the demon king Ravana, as well as honoring the goddess Lakshmi, the deity of wealth and prosperity.

Traditionally, Diwali is celebrated over five days, with families engaging in various rituals such as cleaning and decorating their homes, lighting oil lamps (diyas), and setting off fireworks. Special prayers (pujas) are offered to deities, and families come together to share festive meals that include sweets like ladoos and savory snacks. The atmosphere is filled with joy, laughter, and the spirit of giving.

For diaspora families, Diwali is a cherished occasion that fosters a sense of community and cultural identity. Many organize gatherings with friends and family, host potluck dinners featuring traditional dishes, and participate in local Diwali events. They often decorate their homes with lights and rangoli, ensuring that the essence of this beautiful festival is preserved, even far from home.
